v: An oracle.[^1] The word of Yahweh[^2] to Israel through Malachi.[^3]
מַשָּׂ֥א דְבַר־יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל בְּיַ֖ד מַלְאָכִֽי׃
I have loved you, says Yahweh. But you say, "How have you loved us?" Was not Esau Jacob's brother? declares Yahweh.[^4] Yet I loved Jacob,
אָהַ֤בְתִּי אֶתְכֶם֙ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה וַאֲמַרְתֶּ֖ם בַּמָּ֣ה אֲהַבְתָּ֑נוּ הֲלוֹא־אָ֨ח עֵשָׂ֤ו לְיַֽעֲקֹב֙ נְאֻם־יְהוָ֔ה וָאֹהַ֖ב אֶֽת־יַעֲקֹֽב׃
but Esau I hated.[^5] I have made his mountains a desolation and left his inheritance to the jackals of the desert.
וְאֶת־עֵשָׂ֖ו שָׂנֵ֑אתִי וָאָשִׂ֤ים אֶת־הָרָיו֙ שְׁמָמָ֔ה וְאֶת־נַחֲלָת֖וֹ לְתַנּ֥וֹת מִדְבָּֽר׃

If Edom says, "We have been crushed, but we will rebuild the ruins," this is what Yahweh of Armies[^6] says: They may build, but I will tear down. They will be called the Wicked Country, the people with whom Yahweh is angry forever.

כִּֽי־תֹאמַ֨ר אֱד֜וֹם רֻשַּׁ֗שְׁנוּ וְנָשׁוּב֙ וְנִבְנֶ֣ה חֳרָב֔וֹת כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת הֵ֥מָּה יִבְנ֖וּ וַאֲנִ֣י אֶהֱר֑וֹס וְקָרְא֤וּ לָהֶם֙ גְּב֣וּל רִשְׁעָ֔ה וְהָעָ֛ם אֲשֶׁר־זָעַ֥ם יְהוָ֖ה עַד־עוֹלָֽם׃
Your own eyes will see it, and you will say, "Great is Yahweh beyond the borders of Israel!"
וְעֵינֵיכֶ֖ם תִּרְאֶ֑ינָה וְאַתֶּ֤ם תֹּֽאמְרוּ֙ יִגְדַּ֣ל יְהוָ֔ה מֵעַ֖ל לִגְב֥וּל יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

A son honors his father, and a servant his master. If I am a father, where is the honor due to me? If I am a master, where is the respect due to me? says Yahweh of Armies to you, priests, who despise my name. But you say, "How have we despised your name?"

בֵּ֛ן יְכַבֵּ֥ד אָ֖ב וְעֶ֣בֶד אֲדֹנָ֑יו וְאִם־אָ֣ב אָ֣נִי אַיֵּ֣ה כְבוֹדִ֡י וְאִם־אֲדוֹנִ֣ים אָנִי֩ אַיֵּ֨ה מוֹרָאִ֜י אָמַ֣ר ׀ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֗וֹת לָכֶם֙ הַכֹּֽהֲנִים֙ בּוֹזֵ֣י שְׁמִ֔י וַאֲמַרְתֶּ֕ם בַּמֶּ֥ה בָזִ֖ינוּ אֶת־שְׁמֶֽךָ׃
By offering defiled food[^7] on my altar. But you say, "How have we defiled you?" By saying that the table of Yahweh[^8] may be despised.
מַגִּישִׁ֤ים עַֽל־מִזְבְּחִי֙ לֶ֣חֶם מְגֹאָ֔ל וַאֲמַרְתֶּ֖ם בַּמֶּ֣ה גֵֽאַלְנ֑וּךָ בֶּאֱמָרְכֶ֕ם שֻׁלְחַ֥ן יְהוָ֖ה נִבְזֶ֥ה הֽוּא׃

When you offer blind animals as sacrifices, is that not wrong? When you offer the lame and the sick, is that not wrong?[^9] Try offering them to your governor![^10] Would he be pleased with you or show you favor?[^11] says Yahweh of Armies.
וְכִֽי־תַגִּשׁ֨וּן עִוֵּ֤ר לִזְבֹּ֙חַ֙ אֵ֣ין רָ֔ע וְכִ֥י תַגִּ֛ישׁוּ פִּסֵּ֥חַ וְחֹלֶ֖ה אֵ֣ין רָ֑ע הַקְרִיבֵ֨הוּ נָ֜א לְפֶחָתֶ֗ךָ הֲיִּרְצְךָ֙ א֚וֹ הֲיִשָּׂ֣א פָנֶ֔יךָ אָמַ֖ר יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת׃
So now, plead with God[^12] to be gracious to us! With such offerings from your hands, will he show favor to any of you? says Yahweh of Armies.
וְעַתָּ֛ה חַלּוּ־נָ֥א פְנֵי־אֵ֖ל וִֽיחָנֵ֑נוּ מִיֶּדְכֶם֙ הָ֣יְתָה זֹּ֔את הֲיִשָּׂ֤א מִכֶּם֙ פָּנִ֔ים אָמַ֖ר יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת׃

If only one of you would shut the temple doors, so that you would not light useless fires on my altar! I take no pleasure in you, says Yahweh of Armies, and I will not accept an offering[^13] from your hands.
מִ֤י גַם־בָּכֶם֙ וְיִסְגֹּ֣ר דְּלָתַ֔יִם וְלֹֽא־תָאִ֥ירוּ מִזְבְּחִ֖י חִנָּ֑ם אֵֽין־לִ֨י חֵ֜פֶץ בָּכֶ֗ם אָמַר֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת וּמִנְחָ֖ה לֹֽא־אֶרְצֶ֥ה מִיֶּדְכֶֽם׃

For from the rising of the sun to its setting my name is great among the nations. In every place incense is offered to my name, and a pure offering. For my name is great among the nations, says Yahweh of Armies.[^14]
כִּ֣י מִמִּזְרַח־שֶׁ֜מֶשׁ וְעַד־מְבוֹא֗וֹ גָּד֤וֹל שְׁמִי֙ בַּגּוֹיִ֔ם וּבְכָל־מָק֗וֹם מֻקְטָ֥ר מֻגָּ֛שׁ לִשְׁמִ֖י וּמִנְחָ֣ה טְהוֹרָ֑ה כִּֽי־גָד֤וֹל שְׁמִי֙ בַּגּוֹיִ֔ם אָמַ֖ר יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת׃
But you profane it when you say that the Lord's[^15] table is defiled, and its fruit, its food, may be despised.[^16]
וְאַתֶּ֖ם מְחַלְּלִ֣ים אוֹת֑וֹ בֶּאֱמָרְכֶ֗ם שֻׁלְחַ֤ן אֲדֹנָי֙ מְגֹאָ֣ל ה֔וּא וְנִיב֖וֹ נִבְזֶ֥ה אָכְלֽוֹ׃

And you say, "What a weariness this is!" and you sniff at it,[^17] says Yahweh of Armies. You bring what has been stolen,[^18] and the lame and the sick, and you bring these as an offering! Should I accept it from your hands? says Yahweh.

וַאֲמַרְתֶּם֩ הִנֵּ֨ה מַתְּלָאָ֜ה וְהִפַּחְתֶּ֣ם אוֹת֗וֹ אָמַר֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת וַהֲבֵאתֶ֣ם גָּז֗וּל וְאֶת־הַפִּסֵּ֙חַ֙ וְאֶת־הַ֣חוֹלֶ֔ה וַהֲבֵאתֶ֖ם אֶת־הַמִּנְחָ֑ה הַאֶרְצֶ֥ה אוֹתָ֛הּ מִיֶּדְכֶ֖ם אָמַ֥ר יְהוָֽה׃ ס

Cursed be the cheat who has a male in his flock and vows to give it, but then sacrifices to the Lord one that is blemished! For I am a great King, says Yahweh of Armies, and my name is feared among the nations.
וְאָר֣וּר נוֹכֵ֗ל וְיֵ֤שׁ בְּעֶדְרוֹ֙ זָכָ֔ר וְנֹדֵ֛ר וְזֹבֵ֥חַ מָשְׁחָ֖ת לַֽאדֹנָ֑י כִּי֩ מֶ֨לֶךְ גָּד֜וֹל אָ֗נִי אָמַר֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת וּשְׁמִ֖י נוֹרָ֥א בַגּוֹיִֽם׃

n.1: Hebrew *massa*, from the verb "to lift up, carry": a message "lifted up" by the prophet, or a "burden" laid on a nation. Traditionally "the burden". Compare Zechariah 9:1; 12:1.
n.2: *Yahweh*: God's personal name (Hebrew YHWH), traditionally rendered "the LORD" in English Bibles.
n.3: *Malachi* means "my messenger" (3:1), and may be a title rather than a name. The Septuagint reads "by the hand of his messenger". The book seems to come from the fifth century BC, after the temple had been rebuilt in 515 BC (Ezra 6:15), when a Persian governor ruled Judah (verse 8). It is set out as a series of disputes, in which Yahweh quotes the people's objections and answers them.
n.4: Hebrew *ne'um YHWH*, "the declaration of Yahweh", a formula that marks a prophet's words as Yahweh's own solemn statement.
n.5: The language of choosing: Yahweh chose Jacob and passed over Esau (compare Genesis 25:23; 29:30–31; Deuteronomy 21:15). Romans 9:13 quotes verses 2–3.
n.6: Hebrew *YHWH tseva'ot*, traditionally "the LORD of hosts" or "the LORD Almighty". *Tseva'ot* means armies: the heavenly hosts and the armies of Israel. The title is used more than twenty times in Malachi.
n.7: Literally "defiled bread", the sacrifices offered on the altar as Yahweh's food (Leviticus 21:6).
n.9: Literally "there is no evil", perhaps quoting the priests: "There is nothing wrong with that!" Also later in the verse. The law forbade the offering of animals with defects (Leviticus 22:18–25; Deuteronomy 15:21).
n.10: Hebrew *pechah*, the governor of the Persian province of Judah (Haggai 1:1).
n.12: Literally "soften the face of God", spoken with irony.
n.13: Hebrew *minchah*, "gift, tribute", in Leviticus a grain offering. Also in verses 11 and 13.
n.14: The Hebrew has no verb in the main clauses, so the verse may also be translated in the future: "my name will be great among the nations".
n.15: Hebrew *Adonai*, "the Lord", not the name Yahweh. Also in verse 14.
n.16: Literally "and its fruit is despised, its food". The meaning of the word for fruit, *niv*, is uncertain.
n.17: This is one of the *tiqqune sopherim*, the rabbinic "corrections of the scribes": the tradition says that the text once read "you sniff at me" and was changed out of reverence for God.
n.18: Or "what was torn by wild animals". Hebrew *gazul*, "seized by force".

v: And now, priests, this command is for you.
וְעַתָּ֗ה אֲלֵיכֶ֛ם הַמִּצְוָ֥ה הַזֹּ֖את הַכֹּהֲנִֽים׃

If you will not listen, and if you will not take it to heart to give honor to my name, says Yahweh of Armies,[^1] I will send the curse on you and curse your blessings.[^2] In fact, I have already cursed them, because you are not taking it to heart.

אִם־לֹ֣א תִשְׁמְע֡וּ וְאִם־לֹא֩ תָשִׂ֨ימוּ עַל־לֵ֜ב לָתֵ֧ת כָּב֣וֹד לִשְׁמִ֗י אָמַר֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת וְשִׁלַּחְתִּ֤י בָכֶם֙ אֶת־הַמְּאֵרָ֔ה וְאָרוֹתִ֖י אֶת־בִּרְכֽוֹתֵיכֶ֑ם וְגַם֙ אָרוֹתִ֔יהָ כִּ֥י אֵינְכֶ֖ם שָׂמִ֥ים עַל־לֵֽב׃
Look, I am going to rebuke your offspring,[^3] and I will spread dung on your faces, the dung of your festival sacrifices,[^4] and you will be carried off with it.
הִנְנִ֨י גֹעֵ֤ר לָכֶם֙ אֶת־הַזֶּ֔רַע וְזֵרִ֤יתִי פֶ֙רֶשׁ֙ עַל־פְּנֵיכֶ֔ם פֶּ֖רֶשׁ חַגֵּיכֶ֑ם וְנָשָׂ֥א אֶתְכֶ֖ם אֵלָֽיו׃
Then you will know that I have sent you this command, so that my covenant with Levi may continue,[^5] says Yahweh of Armies.
וִֽידַעְתֶּ֕ם כִּ֚י שִׁלַּ֣חְתִּי אֲלֵיכֶ֔ם אֵ֖ת הַמִּצְוָ֣ה הַזֹּ֑את לִֽהְי֤וֹת בְּרִיתִי֙ אֶת־לֵוִ֔י אָמַ֖ר יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת׃
My covenant with him was one of life and peace, and I gave them to him. It called for reverence, and he revered me and stood in awe of my name.
בְּרִיתִ֣י ׀ הָיְתָ֣ה אִתּ֗וֹ הַֽחַיִּים֙ וְהַ֨שָּׁל֔וֹם וָאֶתְּנֵֽם־ל֥וֹ מוֹרָ֖א וַיִּֽירָאֵ֑נִי וּמִפְּנֵ֥י שְׁמִ֖י נִחַ֥ת הֽוּא׃
True instruction[^6] was in his mouth, and no wrong was found on his lips. He walked with me in peace and uprightness, and he turned many away from wrongdoing.
תּוֹרַ֤ת אֱמֶת֙ הָיְתָ֣ה בְּפִ֔יהוּ וְעַוְלָ֖ה לֹא־נִמְצָ֣א בִשְׂפָתָ֑יו בְּשָׁל֤וֹם וּבְמִישׁוֹר֙ הָלַ֣ךְ אִתִּ֔י וְרַבִּ֖ים הֵשִׁ֥יב מֵעָוֺֽן׃
For the lips of a priest should guard knowledge, and people should seek instruction from his mouth, because he is the messenger[^7] of Yahweh of Armies.
כִּֽי־שִׂפְתֵ֤י כֹהֵן֙ יִשְׁמְרוּ־דַ֔עַת וְתוֹרָ֖ה יְבַקְשׁ֣וּ מִפִּ֑יהוּ כִּ֛י מַלְאַ֥ךְ יְהוָֽה־צְבָא֖וֹת הֽוּא׃
But you have turned aside from the way. You have made many stumble by your instruction. You have corrupted the covenant of Levi, says Yahweh of Armies.
וְאַתֶּם֙ סַרְתֶּ֣ם מִן־הַדֶּ֔רֶךְ הִכְשַׁלְתֶּ֥ם רַבִּ֖ים בַּתּוֹרָ֑ה שִֽׁחַתֶּם֙ בְּרִ֣ית הַלֵּוִ֔י אָמַ֖ר יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת׃
So I in turn have made you despised and humiliated before all the people, because you have not kept my ways but have shown partiality in your instruction.[^8]
וְגַם־אֲנִ֞י נָתַ֧תִּי אֶתְכֶ֛ם נִבְזִ֥ים וּשְׁפָלִ֖ים לְכָל־הָעָ֑ם כְּפִ֗י אֲשֶׁ֤ר אֵֽינְכֶם֙ שֹׁמְרִ֣ים אֶת־דְּרָכַ֔י וְנֹשְׂאִ֥ים פָּנִ֖ים בַּתּוֹרָֽה׃ פ
Have we not all one father?[^9] Has not one God created us? Why then are we faithless to one another,[^10] profaning the covenant of our ancestors?
הֲל֨וֹא אָ֤ב אֶחָד֙ לְכֻלָּ֔נוּ הֲל֛וֹא אֵ֥ל אֶֽחָ֖ד בְּרָאָ֑נוּ מַדּ֗וּעַ נִבְגַּד֙ אִ֣ישׁ בְּאָחִ֔יו לְחַלֵּ֖ל בְּרִ֥ית אֲבֹתֵֽינוּ׃

Judah has been faithless, and a detestable thing has been done in Israel and in Jerusalem. For Judah has profaned the holy place of Yahweh, which he loves,[^11] and has married the daughter of a foreign god.[^12]
בָּגְדָ֣ה יְהוּדָ֔ה וְתוֹעֵבָ֛ה נֶעֶשְׂתָ֥ה בְיִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל וּבִירֽוּשָׁלָ֑͏ִם כִּ֣י ׀ חִלֵּ֣ל יְהוּדָ֗ה קֹ֤דֶשׁ יְהוָה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אָהֵ֔ב וּבָעַ֖ל בַּת־אֵ֥ל נֵכָֽר׃
May Yahweh cut off from the tents of Jacob any man who does this, whoever he may be,[^13] even if he brings an offering to Yahweh of Armies.
יַכְרֵ֨ת יְהוָ֜ה לָאִ֨ישׁ אֲשֶׁ֤ר יַעֲשֶׂ֙נָּה֙ עֵ֣ר וְעֹנֶ֔ה מֵאָהֳלֵ֖י יַֽעֲקֹ֑ב וּמַגִּ֣ישׁ מִנְחָ֔ה לַֽיהוָ֖ה צְבָאֽוֹת׃ פ
And this is another thing you do: you cover the altar of Yahweh with tears, with weeping and groaning, because he no longer looks on the offering or accepts it with pleasure from your hands.
וְזֹאת֙ שֵׁנִ֣ית תַּֽעֲשׂ֔וּ כַּסּ֤וֹת דִּמְעָה֙ אֶת־מִזְבַּ֣ח יְהוָ֔ה בְּכִ֖י וַֽאֲנָקָ֑ה מֵאֵ֣ין ע֗וֹד פְּנוֹת֙ אֶל־הַמִּנְחָ֔ה וְלָקַ֥חַת רָצ֖וֹן מִיֶּדְכֶֽם׃
But you say, "Why?" Because Yahweh has been a witness between you and the wife of your youth, to whom you have been faithless, though she is your companion and your wife by covenant.[^14]
וַאֲמַרְתֶּ֖ם עַל־מָ֑ה עַ֡ל כִּי־יְהוָה֩ הֵעִ֨יד בֵּינְךָ֜ וּבֵ֣ין ׀ אֵ֣שֶׁת נְעוּרֶ֗יךָ אֲשֶׁ֤ר אַתָּה֙ בָּגַ֣דְתָּה בָּ֔הּ וְהִ֥יא חֲבֶרְתְּךָ֖ וְאֵ֥שֶׁת בְּרִיתֶֽךָ׃

Has not the One made them, and are not flesh and spirit his?[^15] And what does the One seek? Godly offspring.[^16] So guard yourselves in your spirit, and let no one be faithless to the wife of his youth.
וְלֹא־אֶחָ֣ד עָשָׂ֗ה וּשְׁאָ֥ר ר֙וּחַ֙ ל֔וֹ וּמָה֙ הָֽאֶחָ֔ד מְבַקֵּ֖שׁ זֶ֣רַע אֱלֹהִ֑ים וְנִשְׁמַרְתֶּם֙ בְּר֣וּחֲכֶ֔ם וּבְאֵ֥שֶׁת נְעוּרֶ֖יךָ אַל־יִבְגֹּֽד׃
For the man who hates and divorces,[^17] says Yahweh, the God of Israel, covers his garment with violence,[^18] says Yahweh of Armies. So guard yourselves in your spirit, and do not be faithless.
כִּֽי־שָׂנֵ֣א שַׁלַּ֗ח אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְכִסָּ֤ה חָמָס֙ עַל־לְבוּשׁ֔וֹ אָמַ֖ר יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֑וֹת וְנִשְׁמַרְתֶּ֥ם בְּרוּחֲכֶ֖ם וְלֹ֥א תִבְגֹּֽדוּ׃ ס

You have wearied Yahweh with your words. But you say, "How have we wearied him?" By saying, "Everyone who does evil is good in the eyes of Yahweh, and he delights in them," or "Where is the God of justice?"
הוֹגַעְתֶּ֤ם יְהוָה֙ בְּדִבְרֵיכֶ֔ם וַאֲמַרְ֖[t]תֶּם בַּמָּ֣ה הוֹגָ֑עְנוּ בֶּאֱמָרְכֶ֗ם כָּל־עֹ֨שֵׂה רָ֜ע ט֣וֹב ׀ בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֗ה וּבָהֶם֙ ה֣וּא חָפֵ֔ץ א֥וֹ אַיֵּ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י הַמִּשְׁפָּֽט׃

n.1: *Yahweh*: God's personal name (Hebrew YHWH), traditionally rendered "the LORD" in English Bibles. *Yahweh of Armies* (Hebrew *YHWH tseva'ot*) is traditionally "the LORD of hosts" or "the LORD Almighty". *Tseva'ot* means armies: the heavenly hosts and the armies of Israel.
n.2: Perhaps the blessings that the priests pronounce on the people (Numbers 6:22–27), or the gifts they receive.
n.3: Hebrew *zera*, "seed, offspring". The same consonants can be read *zeroa*, "arm" or "shoulder", the priests' portion of the sacrifices (Deuteronomy 18:3), and the Septuagint reads "the shoulder".
n.4: Hebrew *peresh*, the dung in the entrails of the sacrificed animals, which was carried out of the camp and burned (Exodus 29:14). *You will be carried off with it* is literally "he will carry you to it".
n.5: Literally "to be my covenant with Levi", the covenant with the priestly tribe (Numbers 25:12–13; Deuteronomy 33:8–11; Jeremiah 33:21).
n.6: Hebrew *torah*, "instruction, teaching, law". Also in verses 7–9.
n.7: Hebrew *mal'akh*, "messenger", the word in Malachi's name (1:1) and in 3:1.
n.8: Literally "lifting faces in the instruction", favoring some people over others when giving rulings.
n.9: Probably God (1:6), or perhaps Abraham or Jacob.
n.11: Or "has profaned what is holy to Yahweh, whom he loves", that is, the people themselves.
n.12: A woman who worships another god. Compare Ezra 9–10; Nehemiah 13:23–27.
n.13: Literally "one who wakes and one who answers", an idiom of uncertain meaning, perhaps "anyone at all".
n.14: Marriage is called a covenant also in Proverbs 2:17 and Ezekiel 16:8.
n.15: The Hebrew of this verse is very difficult, and every translation of it is uncertain. Literally "And not one he made, and a remnant of spirit to him". The text is pointed *she'ar*, "remnant"; the same consonants can be read *she'er*, "flesh", as here. Or "Did he not make them one, with flesh and spirit?" (compare Genesis 2:24), or "No one who has a remnant of the spirit would do this".
n.17: The Hebrew is difficult. Literally "For he hates, send away". Traditionally "For I hate divorce", with a small change to the Hebrew. The Septuagint reads "But if you hate her and send her away".
n.18: Perhaps a picture of marriage, in which a man spread his garment over his wife (Ruth 3:9; Ezekiel 16:8). Here he covers it with violence instead.

v: Look, I am sending my messenger,[^1] and he will prepare the way before me. Then suddenly the Lord[^2] whom you seek will come to his temple, the messenger of the covenant, in whom you delight. Look, he is coming, says Yahweh of Armies.[^3]

הִנְנִ֤י שֹׁלֵחַ֙ מַלְאָכִ֔י וּפִנָּה־דֶ֖רֶךְ לְפָנָ֑י וּפִתְאֹם֩ יָב֨וֹא אֶל־הֵיכָל֜וֹ הָאָד֣וֹן ׀ אֲשֶׁר־אַתֶּ֣ם מְבַקְשִׁ֗ים וּמַלְאַ֨ךְ הַבְּרִ֜ית אֲשֶׁר־אַתֶּ֤ם חֲפֵצִים֙ הִנֵּה־בָ֔א אָמַ֖ר יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת׃
But who can endure the day of his coming? Who can stand when he appears? For he will be like a refiner's fire and like launderers' soap.[^4]
וּמִ֤י מְכַלְכֵּל֙ אֶת־י֣וֹם בּוֹא֔וֹ וּמִ֥י הָעֹמֵ֖ד בְּהֵרָֽאוֹת֑וֹ כִּֽי־הוּא֙ כְּאֵ֣שׁ מְצָרֵ֔ף וּכְבֹרִ֖ית מְכַבְּסִֽים׃
He will sit as a refiner and purifier of silver, and he will purify the sons of Levi[^5] and refine them like gold and silver. Then they will bring offerings[^6] to Yahweh in righteousness.
וְיָשַׁ֨ב מְצָרֵ֤ף וּמְטַהֵר֙ כֶּ֔סֶף וְטִהַ֤ר אֶת־בְּנֵֽי־לֵוִי֙ וְזִקַּ֣ק אֹתָ֔ם כַּזָּהָ֖ב וְכַכָּ֑סֶף וְהָיוּ֙ לַֽיהוָ֔ה מַגִּישֵׁ֥י מִנְחָ֖ה בִּצְדָקָֽה׃
Then the offering of Judah and Jerusalem will be pleasing to Yahweh, as in the days of old and as in former years.
וְעָֽרְבָה֙ לַֽיהוָ֔ה מִנְחַ֥ת יְהוּדָ֖ה וִירֽוּשָׁלָ֑͏ִם כִּימֵ֣י עוֹלָ֔ם וּכְשָׁנִ֖ים קַדְמֹנִיּֽוֹת׃

I will come near to you for judgment. I will be quick to testify against the sorcerers, the adulterers and those who swear falsely, against those who cheat hired workers of their wages[^7] and oppress the widow and the fatherless, and against those who deprive the foreigner of justice and do not fear me, says Yahweh of Armies.

וְקָרַבְתִּ֣י אֲלֵיכֶם֮ לַמִּשְׁפָּט֒ וְהָיִ֣יתִי ׀ עֵ֣ד מְמַהֵ֗ר בַּֽמְכַשְּׁפִים֙ וּבַמְנָ֣אֲפִ֔ים וּבַנִּשְׁבָּעִ֖ים לַשָּׁ֑קֶר וּבְעֹשְׁקֵ֣י שְׂכַר־שָׂ֠כִיר אַלְמָנָ֨ה וְיָת֤וֹם וּמַטֵּי־גֵר֙ וְלֹ֣א יְרֵא֔וּנִי אָמַ֖ר יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת׃
For I, Yahweh, do not change; and you, children of Jacob, have not come to an end.[^8]
כִּ֛י אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה לֹ֣א שָׁנִ֑יתִי וְאַתֶּ֥ם בְּנֵֽי־יַעֲקֹ֖ב לֹ֥א כְלִיתֶֽם׃
From the days of your ancestors you have turned aside from my decrees and have not kept them. Return to me, and I will return to you,[^9] says Yahweh of Armies. But you say, "How shall we return?"
לְמִימֵ֨י אֲבֹתֵיכֶ֜ם סַרְתֶּ֤ם מֵֽחֻקַּי֙ וְלֹ֣א שְׁמַרְתֶּ֔ם שׁ֤וּבוּ אֵלַי֙ וְאָשׁ֣וּבָה אֲלֵיכֶ֔ם אָמַ֖ר יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֑וֹת וַאֲמַרְתֶּ֖ם בַּמֶּ֥ה נָשֽׁוּב׃
Will a human being rob God?[^10] Yet you are robbing me. But you say, "How have we robbed you?" In tithes and contributions.[^11]
הֲיִקְבַּ֨ע אָדָ֜ם אֱלֹהִ֗ים כִּ֤י אַתֶּם֙ קֹבְעִ֣ים אֹתִ֔י וַאֲמַרְתֶּ֖ם בַּמֶּ֣ה קְבַעֲנ֑וּךָ הַֽמַּעֲשֵׂ֖ר וְהַתְּרוּמָֽה׃
You are cursed with a curse, yet you are robbing me, the whole nation of you.
בַּמְּאֵרָה֙ אַתֶּ֣ם נֵֽאָרִ֔ים וְאֹתִ֖י אַתֶּ֣ם קֹבְעִ֑ים הַגּ֖וֹי כֻּלּֽוֹ׃

Bring the whole tithe into the storehouse, so that there may be food in my house. Test me in this, says Yahweh of Armies, and see if I will not open for you the windows of heaven[^12] and pour out for you a blessing until there is no more need.[^13]

הָבִ֨יאוּ אֶת־כָּל־הַֽמַּעֲשֵׂ֜ר אֶל־בֵּ֣ית הָאוֹצָ֗ר וִיהִ֥י טֶ֙רֶף֙ בְּבֵיתִ֔י וּבְחָנ֤וּנִי נָא֙ בָּזֹ֔את אָמַ֖ר יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֑וֹת אִם־לֹ֧א אֶפְתַּ֣ח לָכֶ֗ם אֵ֚ת אֲרֻבּ֣וֹת הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וַהֲרִיקֹתִ֥י לָכֶ֛ם בְּרָכָ֖ה עַד בְּלִי דָֽי׃
I will rebuke the devourer[^14] for you, so that it will not destroy the fruit of your ground, and your vine in the field will not lose its fruit, says Yahweh of Armies.
וְגָעַרְתִּ֤י לָכֶם֙ בָּֽאֹכֵ֔ל וְלֹֽא־יַשְׁחִ֥ת לָכֶ֖ם אֶת־פְּרִ֣י הָאֲדָמָ֑ה וְלֹא־תְשַׁכֵּ֨ל לָכֶ֤ם הַגֶּ֙פֶן֙ בַּשָּׂדֶ֔ה אָמַ֖ר יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת׃
Then all the nations will call you blessed, for you will be a land of delight, says Yahweh of Armies.
וְאִשְּׁר֥וּ אֶתְכֶ֖ם כָּל־הַגּוֹיִ֑ם כִּֽי־תִהְי֤וּ אַתֶּם֙ אֶ֣רֶץ חֵ֔פֶץ אָמַ֖ר יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת׃ ס
Your words have been harsh against me,[^15] says Yahweh. But you say, "What have we said against you?"
חָזְק֥וּ עָלַ֛י דִּבְרֵיכֶ֖ם אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה וַאֲמַרְתֶּ֕ם מַה־נִּדְבַּ֖רְנוּ עָלֶֽיךָ׃
You have said, "It is useless to serve God. What did we gain by keeping his charge[^16] and walking about in mourning before Yahweh of Armies?
אֲמַרְתֶּ֕ם שָׁ֖וְא עֲבֹ֣ד אֱלֹהִ֑ים וּמַה־בֶּ֗צַע כִּ֤י שָׁמַ֙רְנוּ֙ מִשְׁמַרְתּ֔וֹ וְכִ֤י הָלַ֙כְנוּ֙ קְדֹ֣רַנִּ֔ית מִפְּנֵ֖י יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת׃
So now we call the arrogant blessed. Those who do evil not only prosper; they test God and escape."
וְעַתָּ֕ה אֲנַ֖חְנוּ מְאַשְּׁרִ֣ים זֵדִ֑ים גַּם־נִבְנוּ֙ עֹשֵׂ֣י רִשְׁעָ֔ה גַּ֧ם בָּחֲנ֛וּ אֱלֹהִ֖ים וַיִּמָּלֵֽטוּ׃
Then those who feared Yahweh spoke with one another. Yahweh paid attention and heard, and a book of remembrance[^17] was written before him for those who feared Yahweh and honored his name.[^18]
אָ֧ז נִדְבְּר֛וּ יִרְאֵ֥י יְהוָ֖ה אִ֣ישׁ אֶת־רֵעֵ֑הוּ וַיַּקְשֵׁ֤ב יְהוָה֙ וַיִּשְׁמָ֔ע וַ֠יִּכָּתֵב סֵ֣פֶר זִכָּר֤וֹן לְפָנָיו֙ לְיִרְאֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה וּלְחֹשְׁבֵ֖י שְׁמֽוֹ׃
They will be mine, says Yahweh of Armies, my treasured possession,[^19] on the day that I act. I will spare them as a man spares his son who serves him.
וְהָ֣יוּ לִ֗י אָמַר֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת לַיּ֕וֹם אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֲנִ֖י עֹשֶׂ֣ה סְגֻלָּ֑ה וְחָמַלְתִּ֣י עֲלֵיהֶ֔ם כַּֽאֲשֶׁר֙ יַחְמֹ֣ל אִ֔ישׁ עַל־בְּנ֖וֹ הָעֹבֵ֥ד אֹתֽוֹ׃
Then you will again see the difference between the righteous and the wicked, between the one who serves God and the one who does not serve him.
וְשַׁבְתֶּם֙ וּרְאִיתֶ֔ם בֵּ֥ין צַדִּ֖יק לְרָשָׁ֑ע בֵּ֚ין עֹבֵ֣ד אֱלֹהִ֔ים לַאֲשֶׁ֖ר לֹ֥א עֲבָדֽוֹ׃ ס

For look, the day is coming, burning like an oven.[^20] All the arrogant and all who do evil will be stubble, and the day that is coming will set them on fire, says Yahweh of Armies, so that it will leave them neither root nor branch.

כִּֽי־הִנֵּ֤ה הַיּוֹם֙ בָּ֔א בֹּעֵ֖ר כַּתַּנּ֑וּר וְהָי֨וּ כָל־זֵדִ֜ים וְכָל־עֹשֵׂ֤ה רִשְׁעָה֙ קַ֔שׁ וְלִהַ֨ט אֹתָ֜ם הַיּ֣וֹם הַבָּ֗א אָמַר֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת אֲשֶׁ֛ר לֹא־יַעֲזֹ֥ב לָהֶ֖ם שֹׁ֥רֶשׁ וְעָנָֽף׃
But for you who fear my name, the sun of righteousness will rise with healing in its wings.[^21] You will go out and leap like calves let out of the stall.
וְזָרְחָ֨ה לָכֶ֜ם יִרְאֵ֤י שְׁמִי֙ שֶׁ֣מֶשׁ צְדָקָ֔ה וּמַרְפֵּ֖א בִּכְנָפֶ֑יהָ וִֽיצָאתֶ֥ם וּפִשְׁתֶּ֖ם כְּעֶגְלֵ֥י מַרְבֵּֽק׃
You will trample the wicked, for they will be ashes under the soles of your feet on the day that I act, says Yahweh of Armies.
וְעַסּוֹתֶ֣ם רְשָׁעִ֔ים כִּֽי־יִהְי֣וּ אֵ֔פֶר תַּ֖חַת כַּפּ֣וֹת רַגְלֵיכֶ֑ם בַּיּוֹם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אֲנִ֣י עֹשֶׂ֔ה אָמַ֖ר יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת׃ פ
Remember the Law[^22] of Moses my servant, the decrees and rulings that I commanded him at Horeb[^23] for all Israel.
זִכְר֕וּ תּוֹרַ֖ת מֹשֶׁ֣ה עַבְדִּ֑י אֲשֶׁר֩ צִוִּ֨יתִי אוֹת֤וֹ בְחֹרֵב֙ עַל־כָּל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל חֻקִּ֖ים וּמִשְׁפָּטִֽים׃
Look, I am going to send you Elijah the prophet[^24] before the great and terrible day of Yahweh comes.
הִנֵּ֤ה אָֽנֹכִי֙ שֹׁלֵ֣חַ לָכֶ֔ם אֵ֖ת אֵלִיָּ֣ה הַנָּבִ֑יא לִפְנֵ֗י בּ֚וֹא י֣וֹם יְהוָ֔ה הַגָּד֖וֹל וְהַנּוֹרָֽא׃
He will turn the hearts of fathers to their children and the hearts of children to their fathers,[^25] so that I will not come and strike the land with a curse of destruction.[^26]
וְהֵשִׁ֤יב לֵב־אָבוֹת֙ עַל־בָּנִ֔ים וְלֵ֥ב בָּנִ֖ים עַל־אֲבוֹתָ֑ם פֶּן־אָב֕וֹא וְהִכֵּיתִ֥י אֶת־הָאָ֖רֶץ חֵֽרֶם׃

n.1: Hebrew *mal'akhi*, "my messenger", the same word as the name Malachi (1:1). Mark 1:2 quotes this line together with Exodus 23:20, "Look, I am sending my messenger ahead of you. He will prepare your way," and the Gospels apply it to John the Baptist (Matthew 11:10; Luke 7:27). *Prepare* is the verb of Isaiah 40:3, "prepare the way for Yahweh".
n.2: Hebrew *ha-adon*, "the Lord", a title, not the name Yahweh.
n.3: *Yahweh*: God's personal name (Hebrew YHWH), traditionally rendered "the LORD" in English Bibles. *Yahweh of Armies* (Hebrew *YHWH tseva'ot*) is traditionally "the LORD of hosts" or "the LORD Almighty". *Tseva'ot* means armies: the heavenly hosts and the armies of Israel.
n.4: Hebrew *borit*, lye, an alkali used for washing clothes.
n.6: Hebrew *minchah*, "gift, tribute", in Leviticus a grain offering. Also in verse 4.
n.8: Or "you have not stopped being children of Jacob", that is, as deceitful as their ancestor (Genesis 27:36).
n.9: The same words are found in Zechariah 1:3.
n.10: Hebrew *qava*, "rob", a rare verb (Proverbs 22:23). The Septuagint reads "Will a person deceive God?" Also later in the verse and in verse 9.
n.11: Hebrew *terumah*, the portion set apart from the offerings for the priests (Leviticus 7:14; Numbers 18:8–19). The tithes supported the Levites (Numbers 18:21–32; Nehemiah 13:10–12).
n.12: The openings through which the rain was pictured as falling (Genesis 7:11; 2 Kings 7:2).
n.13: Literally "until there is no more enough".
n.15: Literally "Your words have been strong against me".
n.16: Hebrew *mishmeret*, "charge, duty" (Zechariah 3:7). *In mourning* is literally "in black", the clothing of mourners.
n.17: A record of those who belong to Yahweh (compare Exodus 32:32; Psalm 69:29, 69:28 in most English Bibles; Daniel 12:1). The kings of Persia kept such books (Esther 6:1–2).
n.19: Hebrew *segullah*, a king's private treasure, the word used of Israel at Sinai (Exodus 19:5; Deuteronomy 7:6). Or "on the day when I make up my treasured possession".
n.20: Verses 19–24 are 4:1–6 in most English Bibles.
n.21: In the ancient Near East the sun was often pictured as a disk with wings. *Wings* may also mean the rays of the sun. *Righteousness* is Hebrew *tsedaqah*, here the justice that puts right what was wrong.
n.22: Hebrew *torah*, "instruction, teaching, law", here the Law given through Moses as a whole.
n.24: Elijah had been taken up to heaven without dying (2 Kings 2:11). The Gospels see this promise fulfilled in John the Baptist (Matthew 11:14; 17:10–13; Mark 9:11–13; Luke 1:17). *The great and terrible day of Yahweh* is also in Joel 3:4 (2:31 in most English Bibles).
n.25: Luke 1:17 quotes the first half of this line.
n.26: Hebrew *cherem*, the ban by which something was devoted to destruction (Zechariah 14:11). These verses close the Prophets, the second division of the Hebrew Bible, and in most Christian Bibles they close the Old Testament. In the synagogue reading, verse 23 is read again after verse 24, so that the book does not end with a curse.
